reasoning_traces.think:
The risk-constrained Kelly framework modifies the classical Kelly criterion by introducing a risk penalty term through CRRA utility. It enforces a constraint Σ_i p_i W_i^{-λ} ≤ 1, which limits excessive exposure when edge estimates are uncertain. This results in a trade-off between expected growth and risk aversion. The solution preserves the support structure of the unconstrained Kelly, meaning that the same outcomes are selected for betting, but their stakes are scaled down. The calibration process simplifies to solving a one-dimensional root-finding problem on the log scale, making it computationally efficient. The key insight is that even with risk aversion, the fundamental logic of Kelly—betting more on higher edge outcomes—is maintained, just with reduced magnitude. This allows GSE to dynamically adjust to varying levels of confidence in edge estimation without changing the core betting logic.
